text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 1.2% today as crude oil prices remained elevated—Brent hit $106 after a deadly Saudi airport attack, and U.S. oil stayed near $96 per barrel. The refining sector is running at 92.7% capacity, keeping refineries busy and profitable as they convert crude into fuels like diesel and gasoline. This backdrop of tight supply and higher oil prices supports stronger margins for refiners converting raw crude into sellable products.

The stock's broader two-week surge of 18% reflects a shift in the energy outlook: geopolitical tensions around Middle East infrastructure and Russia-Ukraine energy flows have tightened global oil supply, while policy moves (sanctions easing, potential U.S. involvement against Houthis) are keeping crude prices elevated rather than allowing them to fall. For a refiner, higher crude prices can be a double-edged sword, but current refinery utilization and fuel storage levels suggest the industry is capturing value from the supply tightness.
